title.narrative: Revision of the Ghana Housing Sector Profile

description.narrative: The Government of Ghana has requested UN-Habitat to provide technical advisory services to the government through the (Housing Sector Profiles approach) analysis of the housing delivery systems at the city and national levels. The revised housing profile will draw on multi-stakeholder analysis and multi-sector assessment sustained by an action research approach and based on the holistic notion of the housing sector. National experts will be directly involved in the action research. This research includes interviews with key organizations and key local opinion-makers, visits to housing development sites, the implementation of household surveys and public debates involving urban planners, political decision-makers, and private sector and community representatives. This helps to keep the process and outcome of the profile highly pragmatic, while providing multiple opportunities for the strengthening of national expertise and capacity on the issue. While Ghana continues to urbanize (rate at 56.7% now), the demand for adequate, safe, universally accessible, and affordable housing increases exponentially. Inclusive and sustainable policies and programmes can enhance the provision of, and investments in, adequate housing that is connected to livelihood and job opportunities, with access to transportation and other services, and in turn contribute to the reduction of spatial inequalities and urban sprawl. The revised Housing Profile would be the first step to inform and engage policy and decision makers and provide them with evidence needed to design their choices and support critical housing investment decisions. This will inform the functioning of the National Housing Authority to oversee the implementation of the Ghana Housing Policy. Revising the housing profile is a pre-requisite for a broad housing sector reform that aims to improve its overall performance as well as the functioning of its various components and future review of the policy. Access to adequate housing is a precondition for access to employment, education, health, social services and participation in urban and civic life. Inclusive and sustainable policies and programmes can enhance the provision of, and investments in, adequate housing that is connected to livelihood and job opportunities, with access to transportation and other services, and in turn contribute to the reduction of spatial inequalities and urban sprawl. This project proposal reinforces and complements the existing methodologies by supporting the Government of Ghana to conduct a revision of the existing Ghana Housing Profile and use findings to feed into housing policy cycles. To this end, the project aims at revising the Ghana Housing Profile within a structured methodology to support government to effectively: 1) plan and programme housing investments in Ghana and the management and maintenance of activities in areas of housing slum upgrading and prevention 2) support the effective functioning of the proposed National Housing Authority and ultimately inform the country’s works towards the realisation of the right to adequate housing, New Urban Agenda (NUA) and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The learnings from the housing profile review will then feed into the policy cycle and will be used to showcase the linkages and positive impacts of housing interventions on other sectors and policy areas. To this end, the project responds to the needs expressed by the Government of Ghana and other housing stakeholders for effective housing delivery in Ghana to better showcase the cross-sectoral nature of housing and its impact, as a way to advocate for and coordinate integrated investments and joint finance programs across sectors. Additionally, within the UNDSCF in Ghana, data and assessments are highlighted as top priorities to inform evidence-based policy-development, policy coherence, monitoring, evaluation, and learning.
